summary: This is a clinical medical record (office visit note) from Penn Otorhinolaryngology - Head and Neck Surgery, dated August 10, 2022, documenting a 49-year-old male patient's follow-up visit for chronic parotitis and suspected Sjögren's syndrome. The document contains patient history, physical examination findings, MRI sialogram results, and a clinical assessment and plan. It has no relevance to biotech/science project TRL assessment.

content_blocks.title: Office Visit - Chief Complaint & HPI
content_blocks.content: Office visit on Aug 10, 2022 with Dr. Christopher Rassekh, MD at Penn Otorhinolaryngology - Head and Neck Surgery Perelman. Chief Complaint: Follow-up for established patient referred by Dr. Abboud for a history of chronic parotitis. HPI: 49-year-old male with chronic parotitis, fluid behind both ears, high SSA score (>4) on outside lab suggesting Sjögren's syndrome. Reports left-side ear pain around the ear canal, discomfort, no right-side pain but occasional fullness. Feels fluid running from left temple to right face. Hears a sound like fluid with air when pressing on right temple/zygoma and opening mouth. Prior ENT noted fluid was on the left. Ear feels wet. Gets postnasal drip when pushing. Possible wisdom tooth hole, now resolved. Tried Pamabron with little help.

content_blocks.title: Past Medical, Surgical & Family History
content_blocks.content: Past Medical History: 1) Anxiety, 2) Essential hypertension. Past Surgical History: Non-contributory. Family History: Cancer (Mother), Hypertension (Maternal Grandmother), Heart disease (Maternal Grandfather), Cancer (Father). Negative history for Diabetes and Stroke.

content_blocks.title: Physical Examination Findings
content_blocks.content: ENT Physical Exam. Vitals: Pulse 79, Temp 97.7°F (36.5°C), Ht 5'7" (1.702 m), Wt 130 lb (59 kg), SpO2 99%, BMI 20.36 kg/m². General: Well-developed, well-nourished, no acute distress, alert and oriented x3. Oral Cavity: no lesions. Salivary: no masses or definite tenderness, normal flow from all 4 major papillae. Neck: no masses. Lymphatic: no adenopathy. Nose: normal anteriorly. Notable finding: audible click when patient performs the described maneuver. No other abnormalities on exam.

content_blocks.title: Labs and MRI Sialogram Imaging Review
content_blocks.content: Labs: SSA was over 4 on outside lab. Imaging: MRI sialogram performed without contrast. Sequences included Axial T1 weighted, coronal STIR, T2 haste sagittal/oblique left and right, bilateral sagittal and coronal oblique haste, bilateral T2 CISS and SPACE, and bilateral axial oblique haste sequences of the parotid glands. No prior imaging available for comparison. Findings: No abnormality at the site of the skin marker over the right cheek. Salivary glands appear symmetric in signal and size; no evidence of inflammation or focal mass. A focal 2 mm region of signal loss seen along left Stensen's duct (series 7 image 1) — not seen on other sequences; no ductal dilatation; no significant ductal stenosis. Right Stensen's duct appears patent without focal narrowing.

content_blocks.title: Impression, Assessment & Plan
content_blocks.content: Impression: 1) Focal 2 mm region of signal loss along left Stensen's duct — possibly artifactual; if real, could reflect focal narrowing or sialolith. Recommendation: Consider focused ultrasound or unenhanced CT for further evaluation. 2) Bilateral parotid glands appear symmetric without evidence of inflammation or microcysts. Assessment: 1) Jaw clicking, 2) Hypervolemia (unspecified type), 3) Sjögren's syndrome with unspecified organ involvement (CMS-HCC), 4) Hypercalcemia, 5) Parotid duct obstruction, 6) Sinus pressure. Plan: US parotid, CT sinus, PTH/autoimmune labs (SSA >4 on outside lab). Oral surgery consult. Physician noted uncertainty about whether imaging findings or parotid symptoms are related to patient's primary concern about 'fluid' inside his head. Patient reassured; noted to be very anxious. Signed by Christopher H. Rassekh, MD, FACS, Professor of Clinical Otorhinolaryngology-Head & Neck Surgery.
